about: StormSim SF people / life-safety parameters (owned by sim/people.py). Every value has a source; 'assumption' marks planning judgements. Retrieved 25.10.2026.

persons_per_household.source: US Census QuickFacts, San Francisco city/county, 'Persons per household, 2019-2023' (ACS 5-yr) ~2.3, https://www.census.gov/quickfacts/sanfranciscocitycalifornia

gross_m2_per_unit.unit: m2 gross floor area per dwelling unit
gross_m2_per_unit.source: Assumption: SF median apartment ~70 m2 net + ~15% circulation/common area; used only where unit counts are missing

occupied_unit_fraction.source: ACS 2019-2023 5-yr DP04, San Francisco: ~10% housing units vacant

hotel_m2_per_guest.unit: m2 gross hotel floor area per guest
hotel_m2_per_guest.source: Calibrated: SF Travel ~34,000 hotel rooms citywide, majority downtown/SoMa; ~1.5 guests/room at ~80% occupancy; hotel gross area incl. lobbies, conference and F&B ~110 m2/room (Hazus RES4) -> ~90 m2 per guest

worker_m2.unit: m2 gross floor area per daytime occupant (workers + students/visitors)
worker_m2.source: After US EIA CBECS 2018 floorspace per worker by principal building activity (office ~ 30-40 m2/worker nationally; dense SF downtown lower) and Hazus 6.1 occupancy classes; assumption for SF densities

home_fraction_by_hour.unit: share of residents at home, local hour 0-23
home_fraction_by_hour.source: After FEMA Hazus 6.1 Earthquake Technical Manual ch. 13 population distribution (2 AM ~99% residents home, 2 PM ~50-75%, 5 PM commute); assumption interpolated hourly

work_fraction_by_hour.unit: share of daytime occupants present, local hour 0-23
work_fraction_by_hour.source: After FEMA Hazus 6.1 Earthquake Technical Manual ch. 13 (2 PM ~ commercial/industrial fully occupied, 2 AM ~ 2%); assumption interpolated hourly

holiday_work_factor.unit: multiplier on workers present on these dates (MM-DD)
holiday_work_factor.source: Assumption: Christmas Eve / New Year's Eve half staffing, holidays skeleton staffing

no_car_household_share_city.source: ACS 5-yr B25044 'Tenure by vehicles available', San Francisco County: ~31% of households have no vehicle (SFMTA cites ~30%); tract variation scaled by DataSF cne3-h93g poverty share (assumption)

group_size_target.source: Model resolution choice (agents are household/building groups of ~10-50 people)

walk_speed_ms.source: ITE / FHWA design walking speed 4 ft/s (1.2 m/s); MUTCD 2009 sec. 4E.06 uses 3.5 ft/s for signal timing

walk_speed_vulnerable_ms.source: MUTCD 2009 sec. 4E.06: 3.0 ft/s (0.91 m/s) for slower pedestrians (elderly, disabled)

walk_depth_limit_m.source: Abt et al. 1989 (Water Resour. Bull. 25(4)) human stability in flood flows; Defra/EA FD2321 Fig. 3.2: d=0.5 m at low velocity is 'danger for most'; Bernardini et al. 2017 walking speed in floodwater decreases ~linearly with depth

drive_speed_ms.source: Assumption: ~24 km/h urban storm traffic (SFMTA reports Muni/arterial speeds ~13-25 km/h)

car_depth_limit_m.source: NWS 'Turn Around Don't Drown': 12 inches (0.3 m) of moving water can float most cars; 6 in reaches the bottom of most cars, https://www.weather.gov/safety/flood-turn-around-dont-drown

exposed_depth_m.source: Assumption: depth below which a person is not counted as standing in flood water

hr_velocity_const.source: Defra/EA FD2321/TR1 (2006) sec. 3.5: HR = d (v + 0.5) + DF, https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/602bbc768fa8f50383c41f80/Flood_risks_to_people_-_Phase_2_The_flood_risks_to_people_methodology_technical_report.pdf

debris_factor_urban.source: FD2321/TR1 Table 3.1 (urban): 0-0.25 m DF 0; 0.25-0.75 m DF 1; >0.75 m or v>2 DF 1; EA/HR Wallingford Supplementary Note on Flood Hazard Ratings, https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/602d04a98fa8f5037d371a08/FLOOD_HAZARD_RATINGS_AND_THRESHOLDS_explanatory_note.pdf

hr_class_bounds.source: EA/HR Wallingford Supplementary Note (FD2320 thresholds): <0.75 low/caution, 0.75-1.25 danger for some, 1.25-2.0 danger for most, >2.0 danger for all

av_speed_of_onset.source: FD2321/TR1 Table 4.4: rapid flooding = 3 (urban pluvial / sewer surcharge)

av_nature_of_area.source: FD2321/TR1 Table 4.4: multi-storey apartments 1; typical residential/commercial/industrial 2; bungalows, busy roads, parks, single-storey schools 3 (outdoors/moving people use 3)

av_warning_formula.source: FD2321/TR1 Table 4.4: warning score = 3 - P1 (P2 + P3); P1 warning coverage, P2 warning-time target met, P3 effective action. Here P1 = 1 if an alert covers the person, P2 = min(1, lead time / warning_target_s), P3 = 0.5 (assumption)

warning_target_s.source: EA flood warning service target: 2 h lead time before flooding (FD2321 context)

baseline_warning_P.source: Assumption for the no-plan case: generic NWS Flood Watch/Warning reaches ~half of residents with partial lead time (score 2.5)

injury_formula.value: Ninj = 2 * Nz * HR * AV/100 * PV ; Nf = 2 * Ninj * HR/100
injury_formula.source: FD2321/TR1 sec. 6 worked example (Gowdall): Ninj = 2 x Nz x HR x AV/100 x PV, Nf = 2 x Ninj x HR/100; PV = %long-term ill + %aged 75+ (sec. 5.4). Nz = people at ground/basement level in the hazard zone. Peak HR per person over the event.

pv_source_fields.source: DataSF San Francisco Flood Health Vulnerability (cne3-h93g), block-group shares of disabled and elderly residents (proxy for FD2321 long-term ill + aged 75+), https://data.sf.gov/resource/cne3-h93g.json

vsl_usd.source: US DOT Departmental Guidance on Valuation of a Statistical Life in Economic Analysis, 2024 update: VSL $13.7M (2024 dollars) as reported (UMich MJE op-ed May 2025 citing USDOT 2024); prior update $13.2M (2023$) per DHS/USCG VSL memo 9.5.2024 https://www.dco.uscg.mil/Portals/9/VSL%202024%209May24%20FINAL%20for%20DIST.pdf ; DOT page https://www.transportation.gov/office-policy/transportation-policy/revised-departmental-guidance-on-valuation-of-a-statistical-life-in-economic-analysis

injury_vsl_fraction.source: US DOT VSL guidance, AIS/MAIS injury relative values: MAIS 2 (moderate) = 0.047 of VSL (MAIS1 0.003, MAIS3 0.105); flood injuries treated as moderate

rescue_hr_threshold.source: FD2321 'danger for some' threshold: people at or above need assisted evacuation/rescue

shelter_flood_depth_m.source: Assumption: shelter is compromised when water against its walls exceeds its typical first-floor elevation (~0.3 m, buildings.json first_floor_m)

tree_block_height_m.source: Assumption: a failed street tree taller than ~6 m spans a lane (SF residential curb-to-curb 12 m, Better Streets Plan)

vertical_evac_delay_s.source: Assumption: un-warned ground-floor occupants of multi-storey buildings move upstairs ~30 min after water enters (SF DEM / FEMA flood guidance 'go to higher floors'); warned occupants move before water arrives; vulnerable (elderly/disabled) and single-storey occupants cannot

building_depth_quantile.source: Model choice: depth against a building = 75th percentile of street cells within 6 m of its walls (robust to one deep corner)

census_blocks.source: US Census 2020 P.L. 94-171 block POP100 (TIGERweb tigerWMS_Census2020 layer 10); residents per building = block population x share of the block's residential floor area (x fraction of block inside tile)

velocity_cap_ms.source: Model limit for Manning-estimated street flow speed (urban overland flow rarely exceeds ~3 m/s; Russo et al. 2013, Nat. Hazards Earth Syst. Sci. 13, pedestrian stability in urban floods)

slope_cap.source: Model limit on water-surface slope used in the Manning velocity estimate (avoids wet/dry-edge artefacts)

manning_formula.source: Manning (1891) / Chow 1959 Open-Channel Hydraulics; n from data/grid city.npz (Chow 1959 / HEC-RAS 2D manual)

rescue_detour_factor.source: Assumption: street-network distance ~1.3x straight-line (typical urban circuity factor, Ballou et al. 2002, Transportation Research A 36)

walk_min_speed_factor.source: Assumption: wading speed floor (20% of dry walking) below the 0.5 m stop depth

worker_vulnerable_factor.source: Assumption: elderly/disabled share among daytime workers/visitors is ~half the residential share (working-age population)

worker_nocar_factor.source: Assumption: SF downtown commuters mostly arrive by transit (SFMTA/SFCTA: ~50-60% of downtown work trips by transit), so no-car share is higher than residents'

sffd_station_1_xy.source: SFFD Station 1, 935 Folsom St (37.7800 N, 122.4040 W) projected to the grid; staging of baseline SFFD rescue units

warning_P3.source: FD2321/TR1 Table 4.4 P3 (effective action target met): assumption 50% of warned people act effectively
